items.name: Virtual IPs and ARP
items.explanation: A virtual IP is an address that can move between machines. A machine claims it by announcing, with an ARP message, that its network card now answers for that address.

assumedBy.quote: To acquire or release a VIP, a server must send an ARP request.

sources.title: RFC 826: An Ethernet Address Resolution Protocol

items.name: HAProxy
items.explanation: A load balancer and proxy for TCP and HTTP traffic. It sends each connection to a server from its configured pool, and it can reload that pool without dropping traffic.

assumedBy.quote: Thus, a change in Consul to a primary’s identity is observed by each GLB/HAProxy box

sources.title: HAProxy: The Reliable, High Performance TCP/HTTP Load Balancer

items.name: Auto Scaling groups
items.explanation: A set of identical servers that the cloud keeps at a chosen size. If one is lost, the group launches a replacement, and the group can be spread across availability zones.

assumedBy.quote: We run these services in an Auto Scaling group across three or more Availability Zones

sources.title: Auto Scaling groups (Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling)

items.name: Application load balancers
items.explanation: A managed load balancer that spreads HTTP requests across targets in several zones and stops sending to targets whose health checks fail.

assumedBy.quote: The following diagram shows a public-facing Application Load Balancer providing an HTTPS service.

sources.title: What is an Application Load Balancer?

items.name: Regions and availability zones
items.explanation: A cloud region is made of several availability zones, which are separate data centres with their own power and network. Spreading across zones survives the loss of one.

assumedBy.quote: Availability Zones are logically isolated sections of an AWS Region
